title: Refactor GPU autoscaler: consolidate node lifecycle and cleanup capacity planner
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
We are removing long-standing technical debt in the GPU fleet autoscaler: consolidate scattered node lifecycle code, simplify capacity planner heuristics, and upgrade k8s client dependencies to remove flaky describe/list hotspots. Goals are to reduce scale-up latency variance, eliminate occasional OOMs during large cluster snapshots, and make future autoscaling fixes tractable by centralizing logic into a new NodeManager component.

Technical highlights / changes planned:
- Capacity planner cleanup: remove the legacy double-counting path that caused transient overcommit behavior; unify capacity accounting into a single pass that uses stable snapshots and fieldSelectors to minimize API payloads.
- Node lifecycle refactor: extract node provisioning, annotation, and termination code from autoscaler/scale_handler into runtime/node_manager. NodeManager will own state transitions and expose a clean interface for the autoscaler and for the Dedicated allocator.
- Dependency upgrades: bump k8s client-go from v0.26 -> v0.28, upgrade controller-runtime to match, and migrate away from deprecated ListOptions fields. This addresses noisy warnings and improves compatibility with newer GKE/AKS clusters.
- Performance fixes: replace a global coarse-locked cache with per-pool sharded locks to reduce mutex contention under high request churn; backpressure requests when KV-cache becomes hot.
- API optimization: switch heavy node snapshot operations to use pagination + fieldSelectors to avoid listing entire node objects; reduce frequency of full cluster lists from 10s to 30s with event-driven diffs.
- Observability & safety: add histograms for scaleUpLatency, capacityDelta, and nodeLifecycleDuration; expose canary dashboards in Grafana and add alert rules for unexpected capacity drift > 5% for > 5 minutes.

Why now:
- Multiple incidents in Q4 2025 showed autoscaler OOMs and scale-up jitter when handling 1000+ node clusters. The current code is brittle for large Dedicated pools and makes future features (burst capacity, preemption awareness) risky.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit coverage for NodeManager state transitions >= 90% for critical paths.
- End-to-end load test demonstrates 30% reduction in 95th percentile scale-up latency on a 500-node synthetic workload.
- No regressions in canary (1 cluster) for 72 hours after rollout.
- Decrease memory usage of autoscaler process by at least 25% under benchmark.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge NodeManager behind feature flag runtime.node_manager.v1 and run in shadow mode on staging clusters.
2) Canary rollout to 1 Dedicated region (canary pool) with feature flag enabled for autoscaler leader only. Monitor dashboard + error budget for 72 hours.
3) Gradual ramp: 10% -> 50% -> 100% of Dedicated pools over 7 days if thresholds pass.
4) Quick rollback via killing feature flag and reverting leader selection to previous autoscaler.

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for capacity accounting and state machine transitions.
- Integration: local k8s kind tests that simulate node join/terminate sequences and scale events.
- Load test: run synthetic 500-node + 2000-request burst scenario; capture prometheus histograms and memory profiles.
- Chaos: simulate API server high latency and ensure autoscaler does not double-request nodes.

Migration notes / backward compatibility:
- NodeManager is initially non-destructive and only claims nodes via annotations; behavior identical to previous implementation when feature flag is off.
- The database schema used by capacity planner remains unchanged; we add a migration that is read-only until the final cutover.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: k8s client upgrade could surface incompatibilities with older clusters. Mitigation: run compatibility matrix in CI and hold an allowlist for older clusters.
- Risk: transient capacity underprovisioning during rollout. Mitigation: conservative canary threshold and immediate rollback path; maintain burst-capacity circuit-breaker to fallback to previous allocator.

Open design decisions:
- Whether NodeManager should expose an HTTP debug API (we currently lean yes for operational debugging, but will gate behind RBAC).
- Final sharding key for per-pool locks: pool-id vs node-label. (Design doc proposes pool-id; awaiting feedback from infra).

References / artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/NodeManager+and+Capacity+Planner+Refactor
- Load test dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abc123/autoscaler-load-tests
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5832, https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5879
- Incident notes: https://docs.redwood.ai/incident/2025-11-autoscaler-oom

Next steps / immediate TODOs:
- Finish client-go upgrade subtree and run CI matrix (assigned).
- Complete NodeManager shadow mode implementation and smoke tests.
- Add histograms + Grafana panels before canary merge.
